subject: zoology_2
question_text: Bile juice contains no digestive enzymes, yet it is important for digestion. How?

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book p.46, VSAQ 50. The printed exam years are the book's claim, reproduced here as appearances. Zoology-II holds only ONE source book in the corpus, so the two-book union check is structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is our reading of the question and is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Revised 2026-09-05: the insider note, s1_emulsify's margin note and its second common mistake all stated which word carries or loses a mark, so each now gives the reason instead — bile salts break the fat into small droplets rather than digesting it.

insider_note: Emulsify is the word this answer turns on. Bile has no enzyme, so it does not digest fat: the bile salts break the fat into very small micelles, and bile then activates lipase.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Bile salts emulsify fats
steps.why: Fat and water do not mix, so a large fat drop offers very little surface for an enzyme to work on until it is broken up.
common_mistakes: Writing that bile digests fat. It only breaks the fat into small drops.
Leaving out the word emulsify. Bile salts do not digest the fat; they break it into very small droplets.
steps.memory_tip: Bile is the soap of the gut: it breaks fat into small drops.
steps.margin_note: Two lines. Emulsify is the word the answer turns on.

steps.why: Bile does the two jobs an enzyme cannot do for itself: it exposes the fat and it switches the enzyme on.
